facts.value: Christianity is based on the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth (1st century) as presented in the New Testament.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: The Christian faith is essentially faith in Jesus as the Christ, the Son of God, and as Savior and Lord.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Almost all Christians believe in the Trinity, which teaches the unity of Father, Son (Jesus Christ), and Holy Spirit as three persons in one Godhead.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Most Christians can describe their faith with the Nicene Creed.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Christianity was the religion of the Byzantine Empire in the first millennium and of Western Europe during the time of colonization.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Christianity is the world's largest religion, with about 2.3 billion followers as of 2015.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: The main divisions of Christianity include Catholicism, Eastern Christianity, and Protestantism.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: The Catholic Church is led by the Bishop of Rome and includes 24 Churches sui iuris, such as the Latin Church and 23 Eastern Catholic churches.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Eastern Christianity includes Eastern Orthodoxy, Oriental Orthodoxy, and the Church of the East.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Protestantism separated from the Catholic Church in the 16th-century Protestant Reformation and is split into thousands of denominations, including major branches like Anglicanism, Baptists, Calvinism, Lutheranism, and Methodism.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Smaller groups include Restorationism, the Latter-day Saint movement, and Jehovah's Witnesses.
